newsitem.title: FRANCE: GIA leader warns of more killings in Algeria-paper.
newsitem.headline: GIA leader warns of more killings in Algeria-paper.

text.p: Algeria's ruthless Armed Islamic Group (GIA) said in a statement published on Monday that it had launched a new stage of killings in the North African country's cities and villages.
GIA leader Antar Zouabri also said Algerian forces had started a second offensive against the GIA's main mountainous stronghold on February 19 after an early operation against its "failed".

Zouabri, quoted by the London-based al-Hayat Arabic newspaper, said: "A new stage of fighting with the government has started with the killing of the apostates and their relatives in cities and villagers and bombings in the hearts of Algiers and Blida."
Algiers and the nearby garrison town of Blida regions bore the brunt of a series of bomb attacks and massacres during the past month, coinciding largely with the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
Zouabri then had reportedly promised to step up killings against "all (those) who are not with us".

Over the past few days suspected Moslem guerrillas have killed 12 people, including five members of one family, Algerian newspapers reported on Monday. The five, including twin sisters aged 22, had their throats slit on Friday night in the family home in Laghouat, 340 km (210 miles) south of Algiers.

Besides the GIA the main other rebel group is Algeria's Islamic Salvation Army -- armed wing of the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) -- which said last week it had killed over 180 security force members in recent clashes.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the FIS, later banned, had taken a huge lead.
Zouabri's latest statement, dated February 22 and quoted by al-Hayat, said paratroopers, backed by tanks, had attacked the GIA stronghold in mountainous Chrea, overlooking Blida.
It said "as the January 16 offensive failed, the security forces renewed the attack on February 19 which was supervised by Lieutenant-General Mohamed Lamari.
"Artillery and gunships took part in bombarding the area where helicopters carried out four attacks," said the statement. It gave no further details.
Last week, security forces in simultaneous operations in Medea and Chrea regions killed 60 guerrillas, said El Watan newspaper on Sunday, quoting what it called reliable sources.

El Watan made no mention of casualties among the security forces but Zouabri was quoted by al-Hayat as saying that "many security force members have been killed and who wants evidence has to go to hospitals in Algiers and Medea".
More than 150 villagers have been slaughtered in the past four months in Chrea and Medea in raids the authorities blame on Moslem guerrillas.
In the latest attack, 33 people were hacked to death 11 days ago in Kerrach hamlet in Chrea area, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
Zouabri was quoted on Monday by al-Hayat as taking responsibility for this massacre and an unreported mass killing of villagers in nearby Bougara area.
President Liamine Zeroual was quoted earlier this month as saying that much of the latest wave of killings was a result of in-fighting among rival guerrilla factions.
